newsitem.title: CHINA: China dissident in bold call for democratic reform.
newsitem.headline: China dissident in bold call for democratic reform.

text.p: Chinese dissident Qin Yongmin has made a bold call for a crucial forthcoming Communist Party congress to embrace democratic reforms.

Qin said on Tuesday he had written to Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin, urging the introduction of county-level elections and the lifting of a ban on political debate in the local media before the end of the century.
He called on Jiang to introduce provincial- and central government-level elections and guarantee the freedom to stage street protests and labour strikes in the next century.
"I hope Jiang Zemin will have the courage ... to engage in reform of the political system at the 15th party congress," Qin said in his letter, a copy of which was made available to reporters.
China's communist leaders will hold a five-yearly party congress in late September or early October to set the path of the world's most populous nation into the 21st century.
Qin said he expected repercussions, but was undaunted. "Danger is unavoidable ... but I'm not afraid," Qin said by telephone from his home in the central city of Wuhan.

The 44-year-old former steel worker was jailed for seven years in 1981 for spreading counter-revolutionary, or subversive, propaganda and for incitement after taking part in the Democracy Wall movement.
He penned a "peace charter" in 1993, landing him two years in a labour camp. He accused labour camp guards of beating him up and crushing one of his testicles.
Last week Beijing University economics professor Shang Dewen called for Western-style democratic reforms, urging the introduction of direct elections for state president and for provincial governors.
